sanskrit: dyāṃ dharāṃ khaṃ diśo vāri pradiśaś cānunādayan aho dhig iti bhūtānāṃ śabdaḥ samabhavan mahān
english: Making heaven, earth, the sky, the quarters, the waters, and the intermediate regions resound, a great cry went up from all beings: "Alas! Shame!"

sanskrit: devatāḥ pitaraś caiva pūrve ye cāsya bāndhavāḥ dadṛśur nihataṃ tatra bhāradvājaṃ mahāratham
english: The gods, the ancestral fathers, and those who had been his kinsmen of old looked down and beheld Bhāradvāja, that mighty warrior, lying slain.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu jayaṃ labdhvā siṃhanādān pracakrire tena nādena mahatā samakampata medinī
english: The Pāṇḍavas, having won the victory, raised lion-roars, and at that mighty roar the whole earth trembled.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kiṃ kurvāṇaṃ raṇe droṇaṃ jaghnuḥ pāṇḍavasṛñjayāḥ tathā nipuṇam astreṣu sarvaśastrabhṛtām api
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: While Droṇa was doing what in battle did the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas slay him — him so skilled in weapons, foremost among all who bear arms?

sanskrit: rathabhaṅgo babhūvāsya dhanur vāśīryatāsyataḥ pramatto vābhavad droṇas tato mṛtyum upeyivān
english: Did his chariot break apart, or did his bow shatter as he shot, or did Droṇa grow heedless, that he thus met his death?

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu pārṣatas tāta śatrubhir duṣpradharṣaṇam kirantam iṣusaṃghātān rukmapuṅkhān anekaśaḥ
english: How, my son, did the son of Pṛṣata strike down one whom foes could not assail, who scattered showers of gold-feathered arrows in their thousands —

sanskrit: kṣiprahastaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ kṛtinaṃ citrayodhinam dūreṣupātinaṃ dāntam astrayuddhe ca pāragam
english: that swift-handed best of brahmins, the accomplished one, the dazzling fighter, who struck from afar, the self-controlled, the master of warfare with divine weapons?

sanskrit: pāñcālaputro nyavadhīd diṣṭyā sa varam acyutam kurvāṇaṃ dāruṇaṃ karma raṇe yattaṃ mahāratham
english: By cruel fate the Pāñcāla prince slew that unfaltering, supreme warrior, who was performing terrible deeds and striving with all his might in the battle.

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ diṣṭaṃ hi balavat pauruṣād iti me matiḥ yad droṇo nihataḥ śūraḥ pārṣatena mahātmanā
english: Surely destiny is mightier than human valor — this is my conviction — since the hero Droṇa was slain by the great-souled son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: astraṃ caturvidhaṃ vīre yasminn āsīt pratiṣṭhitam tam iṣvastravarācāryaṃ droṇaṃ śaṃsasi me hatam
english: In that hero the fourfold science of weapons was firmly established; yet you tell me that Droṇa, the supreme teacher of archery, is slain.

sanskrit: śrutvā hataṃ rukmarathaṃ vaiyāghraparivāraṇam jātarūpapariṣkāraṃ nādya śokam apānude
english: Hearing that he of the golden chariot is slain — he whose car was draped with tiger-skins and adorned with gold — I cannot today drive away my grief.

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ paraduḥkhena kaś cin mriyati saṃjaya yatra droṇam ahaṃ śrutvā hataṃ jīvāmi na mriye
english: Surely no one dies of another's sorrow, Saṃjaya, since I, having heard that Droṇa is slain, still live and do not die.

sanskrit: aśmasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ mama yac chrutvā nihataṃ droṇaṃ śatadhā na vidīryate
english: Surely my heart is made of iron, exceedingly hard, that it does not burst into a hundred pieces on hearing that Droṇa is slain.

sanskrit: brāhme vede tatheṣv astre yam upāsan guṇārthinaḥ brāhmaṇā rājaputrāś ca sa kathaṃ mṛtyunā hataḥ
english: He whom brahmins and princes seeking excellence waited upon in the sacred Veda, in archery, and in divine weapons — how was he struck down by death?

sanskrit: śoṣaṇaṃ sāgarasyeva meror iva visarpaṇam patanaṃ bhāskarasyeva na mṛṣye droṇapātanam
english: Like the drying-up of the ocean, like the toppling of Meru, like the falling of the sun — I cannot bear the felling of Droṇa.

sanskrit: dṛptānāṃ pratiṣeddhāsīd dhārmikānāṃ ca rakṣitā yo 'tyākṣīt kṛpaṇasyārthe prāṇān api paraṃtapaḥ
english: He was the curber of the arrogant and the protector of the righteous, that scorcher of foes who would lay down even his life for the sake of the helpless.

sanskrit: mandānāṃ mama putrāṇāṃ jayāśā yasya vikrame bṛhaspatyuśanastulyo buddhyā sa nihataḥ katham
english: He in whose prowess lay the hope of victory for my dull-witted sons, the equal of Bṛhaspati and Uśanas in wisdom — how was he slain?

sanskrit: te ca śoṇā bṛhanto 'śvāḥ saindhavā hemamālinaḥ rathe vātajavā yuktāḥ sarvaśabdātigā raṇe
english: And those tall red horses of the Sindhu breed, garlanded with gold, swift as the wind, yoked to his chariot, unshaken by every clamor of battle —

sanskrit: balino ghoṣiṇo dāntāḥ saindhavāḥ sādhuvāhinaḥ dṛḍhāḥ saṃgrāmamadhyeṣu kaccid āsan na vihvalāḥ
english: strong, loud-neighing, well-trained Sindhu steeds, drawing smoothly, steadfast in the thick of the fray — were they perhaps thrown into confusion?

sanskrit: kariṇāṃ bṛṃhatāṃ yuddhe śaṅkhadundubhinisvanam jyākṣepaśaravarṣāṇāṃ śastrāṇāṃ ca sahiṣṇavaḥ
english: They could endure in battle the trumpeting of elephants, the blare of conches and kettledrums, the twang of bowstrings, the showers of arrows, and the clash of weapons —

sanskrit: āśaṃsantaḥ parāñ jetuṃ jitaśvāsā jitavyathāḥ hayāḥ prajavitāḥ śīghrā bhāradvājarathodvahāḥ
english: those horses that bore Bhāradvāja's chariot, eager to conquer the foe, masters of their own breath, mastering all pain, swift and urged to speed.

sanskrit: te sma rukmarathe yuktā naravīrasamāhitāḥ kathaṃ nābhyataraṃs tāta pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: Yoked to the golden chariot, set in motion by that hero among men — how, my son, did they fail to break through the host of the Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: jātarūpapariṣkāram āsthāya ratham uttamam bhāradvājaḥ kim akaroc chūraḥ saṃkrandano yudhi
english: Mounted upon his excellent chariot adorned with gold, what did the heroic, war-shouting Bhāradvāja do in the battle?

sanskrit: vidyāṃ yasyopajīvanti sarvalokadhanurbhṛtaḥ sa satyasaṃdho balavān droṇaḥ kim akarod yudhi
english: He upon whose learning all the bowmen of the world depend — that strong Droṇa, true to his vows, what did he do in the fight?

sanskrit: divi śakram iva śreṣṭhaṃ mahāmātraṃ dhanurbhṛtām ke nu taṃ raudrakarmāṇaṃ yuddhe pratyudyayū rathāḥ
english: He who was foremost among bowmen as Śakra is in heaven, that mighty one — what warriors in their chariots dared advance against him of terrible deeds in battle?

sanskrit: nanu rukmarathaṃ dṛṣṭvā pradravanti sma pāṇḍavāḥ divyam astraṃ vikurvāṇaṃ senāṃ kṣiṇvantam avyayam
english: Surely, on seeing him of the golden chariot wielding divine weapons and thinning their inexhaustible army, the Pāṇḍavas would flee?

sanskrit: utāho sarvasainyena dharmarājaḥ sahānujaḥ pāñcālyapragraho droṇaṃ sarvataḥ samavārayat
english: Or did the King of Righteousness, together with his younger brothers and with the Pāñcāla prince at their head, with his whole army surround Droṇa on every side?

sanskrit: nūnam āvārayat pārtho rathino 'nyān ajihmagaiḥ tato droṇaṃ samārohat pārṣataḥ pāpakarmakṛt
english: Surely Pārtha held off the other chariot-warriors with his straight-flying shafts, and then the son of Pṛṣata, doer of an evil deed, fell upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: na hy anyaṃ paripaśyāmi vadhe kaṃ cana śuṣmiṇaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnād ṛte raudrāt pālyamānāt kirīṭinā
english: For I can see no other capable of slaying that valiant one except the fierce Dhṛṣṭadyumna, guarded as he was by the Diademed Arjuna.

sanskrit: tair vṛtaḥ sarvataḥ śūraiḥ pāñcālyāpasadas tataḥ kekayaiś cedikārūṣair matsyair anyaiś ca bhūmipaiḥ
english: Then that base-born Pāñcāla, surrounded on all sides by those heroes — by the Kekayas, the Cedis, the Kārūṣas, the Matsyas, and other kings —

sanskrit: vyākulīkṛtam ācāryaṃ pipīlair uragaṃ yathā karmaṇy asukare saktaṃ jaghāneti matir mama
english: slew the teacher, who had been thrown into confusion as a serpent is by ants, while he was engaged in a deed hard to perform — such is my belief.

sanskrit: yo 'dhītya caturo vedān sarvān ākhyānapañcamān brāhmaṇānāṃ pratiṣṭhāsīt srotasām iva sāgaraḥ sa kathaṃ brāhmaṇo vṛddhaḥ śastreṇa vadham āptavān
english: He who, having studied the four Vedas together with the legends as a fifth, stood as the refuge of brahmins as the ocean is of streams — how did that aged brahmin meet his death by the sword?

sanskrit: amarṣaṇo marṣitavān kliśyamānaḥ sadā mayā anarhamāṇaḥ kaunteyaḥ karmaṇas tasya tat phalam
english: Impatient by nature, he yet bore patiently, though ever harassed by me. The son of Kuntī, who deserved no such treatment, has reaped the fruit of that conduct.

sanskrit: yasya karmānujīvanti loke sarvadhanurbhṛtaḥ sa satyasaṃdhaḥ sukṛtī śrīkāmair nihataḥ katham
english: He on whose accomplishment all the bowmen in the world depend for their livelihood — that virtuous one, true to his word, how was he slain by men greedy for glory?

sanskrit: divi śakra iva śreṣṭho mahāsattvo mahābalaḥ sa kathaṃ nihataḥ pārthaiḥ kṣudramatsyair yathā timiḥ
english: He who was foremost as Śakra is in heaven, of great courage and great strength — how was he slain by the sons of Pṛthā, as a great whale is slain by little fishes?

sanskrit: kṣiprahastaś ca balavān dṛḍhadhanvārimardanaḥ na yasya jīvitākāṅkṣī viṣayaṃ prāpya jīvati
english: Swift-handed and strong, with a stout bow, a crusher of foes, into whose range no one desiring to live could come and yet live —

sanskrit: yaṃ dvau na jahataḥ śabdau jīvamānaṃ kadā cana brāhmaś ca vedakāmānāṃ jyāghoṣaś ca dhanurbhṛtām
english: whom, while he lived, two sounds never left: the chant of the Veda for those who sought sacred lore, and the twang of the bowstring for those who bear arms.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ mṛṣye hataṃ droṇaṃ siṃhadviradavikramam kathaṃ saṃjaya durdharṣam anādhṛṣyayaśobalam
english: I cannot bear that Droṇa is slain — he of the prowess of a lion or an elephant. How, Saṃjaya, did this unassailable one, of unconquerable fame and might, fall?

sanskrit: ke 'rakṣan dakṣiṇaṃ cakraṃ savyaṃ ke ca mahātmanaḥ purastāt ke ca vīrasya yudhyamānasya saṃyuge
english: Who guarded the right wheel of that great soul, and who the left, and who stood before the hero as he fought in the encounter?

sanskrit: ke ca tatra tanuṃ tyaktvā pratīpaṃ mṛtyum āvrajan droṇasya samare vīrāḥ ke 'kurvanta parāṃ dhṛtim
english: And what heroes there, casting away their bodies, went forth to meet death head-on, what warriors showed the highest resolve in Droṇa's battle?

sanskrit: etad āryeṇa kartavyaṃ kṛcchrāsv āpatsu saṃjaya parākramed yathāśaktyā tac ca tasmin pratiṣṭhitam
english: This is what a noble man must do in dire calamities, Saṃjaya — to strive with all his power; and that was firmly established in him.

sanskrit: muhyate me manas tāta kathā tāvan nivartyatām bhūyas tu labdhasaṃjñas tvā pariprakṣyāmi saṃjaya
english: My mind grows faint, my son; let the narration pause awhile. When I have regained my senses, I shall question you again, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ pṛṣṭvā sūtaputraṃ hṛcchokenārdito bhṛśam jaye nirāśaḥ putrāṇāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'patat kṣitau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus questioned the sūta's son, sorely afflicted with grief of heart and despairing of his sons' victory, Dhṛtarāṣṭra fell to the ground.

sanskrit: taṃ visaṃjñaṃ nipatitaṃ siṣicuḥ paricārakāḥ jalenātyarthaśītena vījantaḥ puṇyagandhinā
english: As he lay fallen and senseless, the attendants sprinkled him with exceedingly cool, fragrant water and fanned him.

sanskrit: patitaṃ cainam ājñāya samantād bharatastriyaḥ parivavrur mahārājam aspṛśaṃś caiva pāṇibhiḥ
english: Aware that he had fallen, the women of the Bharatas gathered round the great king on every side and touched him with their hands.

sanskrit: utthāpya cainaṃ śanakai rājānaṃ pṛthivītalāt āsanaṃ prāpayām āsur bāṣpakaṇṭhyo varāṅganāḥ
english: Slowly raising the king from the surface of the earth, those lovely women, their throats choked with tears, brought him to his seat.

sanskrit: āsanaṃ prāpya rājā tu mūrchayābhipariplutaḥ niśceṣṭo 'tiṣṭhata tadā vījyamānaḥ samantataḥ
english: Having reached his seat, the king, overwhelmed by a swoon, remained motionless, while he was fanned on every side.

sanskrit: sa labdhvā śanakaiḥ saṃjñāṃ vepamāno mahīpatiḥ punar gāvalgaṇiṃ sūtaṃ paryapṛcchad yathātatham
english: Slowly regaining consciousness, the trembling lord of the earth questioned the sūta, son of Gavalgaṇa, once more, point by point.

sanskrit: yat tad udyann ivādityo jyotiṣā praṇudaṃs tamaḥ āyād ajātaśatrur vai kas taṃ droṇād avārayat
english: When Ajātaśatru advanced, dispelling the darkness with his radiance like the rising sun, who held him back from Droṇa?

sanskrit: prabhinnam iva mātaṅgaṃ tathā kruddhaṃ tarasvinam āsaktamanasaṃ dīptaṃ pratidviradaghātinam vāśitāsaṃgame yadvad ajayyaṃ pratiyūthapaiḥ
english: Like a rutting elephant, thus enraged and swift, his mind fixed on the foe, blazing, slaying the elephants that opposed him — unconquerable by rival herd-leaders as in the rivalry for a cow-elephant —

sanskrit: ati cānyān raṇe yodhān vīraḥ puruṣasattamaḥ yo hy eko hi mahābāhur nirdahed ghoracakṣuṣā kṛtsnaṃ duryodhanabalaṃ dhṛtimān satyasaṃgaraḥ
english: surpassing the other warriors in battle, that hero, best of men, the mighty-armed, who alone, steadfast and true to his oath, could burn up Duryodhana's whole host with the mere glare of his terrible eyes —

sanskrit: cakṣurhaṇaṃ jaye saktam iṣvāsavararakṣitam dāntaṃ bahumataṃ loke ke śūrāḥ paryavārayan
english: him whose gaze could destroy, bent upon victory, guarded by the best of bowmen, self-controlled and honored throughout the world — what heroes hemmed him in?

sanskrit: ke duṣpradharṣaṃ rājānam iṣvāsavaram acyutam samāsedur naravyāghraṃ kaunteyaṃ tatra māmakāḥ
english: What men of mine there closed in upon that unassailable king, the best of bowmen, the unfaltering, that tiger among men, the son of Kuntī?

sanskrit: tarasaivābhipatyātha yo vai droṇam upādravat taṃ bhīmasenam āyāntaṃ ke śūrāḥ paryavārayan
english: He who, charging swiftly, fell upon Droṇa — what heroes surrounded that Bhīmasena as he came on?

sanskrit: yad āyāj jaladaprakhyo rathaḥ paramavīryavān parjanya iva bībhatsus tumulām aśaniṃ sṛjan
english: When Bībhatsu advanced, his chariot dark as a rain-cloud, of supreme valor, hurling tumultuous thunderbolts like Parjanya —

sanskrit: vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi varṣāṇi maghavān iva iṣusaṃbādham ākāśaṃ kurvan kapivaradhvajaḥ avasphūrjan diśaḥ sarvās talanemisvanena ca
english: he of the monkey-bannered standard rained down showers of arrows as Maghavān rains the rains, choking the sky with shafts and making all the quarters crash with the din of his palm-guards and wheel-rims —

sanskrit: cāpavidyutprabho ghoro rathagulmabalāhakaḥ rathanemighoṣastanitaḥ śaraśabdātibandhuraḥ
english: terrible, his bow flashing like lightning, his chariot-squadrons a thundercloud, thundering with the roar of his chariot-rims, made fearsome by the rush of arrows —

sanskrit: roṣanirjitajīmūto mano 'bhiprāyaśīghragaḥ marmātigo bāṇadhāras tumulaḥ śoṇitodakaḥ
english: his fury surpassing the storm-clouds, moving swift as thought, a downpour of arrows that pierced the vitals, tumultuous, with blood for its waters —

sanskrit: saṃplāvayan mahīṃ sarvāṃ mānavair āstaraṃs tadā gadāniṣṭanito raudro duryodhanakṛtodyamaḥ
english: flooding the whole earth and strewing it with the slain, fierce, resounding with the clash of maces, roused up by Duryodhana's doing —

sanskrit: yuddhe 'bhyaṣiñcad vijayo gārdhrapatraiḥ śilāśitaiḥ gāṇḍīvaṃ dhārayan dhīmān kīdṛśaṃ vo manas tadā
english: when the wise Vijaya in that battle, wielding the Gāṇḍīva, bathed the field with vulture-feathered shafts honed on stone — what then was the temper of your minds?

sanskrit: kaccid gāṇḍīvaśabdena na praṇaśyata vai balam yad vaḥ sa bhairavaṃ kurvann arjuno bhṛśam abhyagāt
english: Did not your army perish at the sound of the Gāṇḍīva, when Arjuna, raising that fearful roar, bore down upon you in fury?

sanskrit: kaccin nāpānudad droṇād iṣubhir vo dhanaṃjayaḥ vāto meghān ivāvidhyan pravāñ śaravanānilaḥ ko hi gāṇḍīvadhanvānaṃ naraḥ soḍhuṃ raṇe 'rhati
english: Did not Dhanaṃjaya drive you back from Droṇa with his shafts, scattering you with a forest-felling wind of arrows as the gale scatters clouds? What man is able to withstand the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva in battle?

sanskrit: yat senāḥ samakampanta yad vīrān aspṛśad bhayam ke tatra nājahur droṇaṃ ke kṣudrāḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: When the armies trembled and fear laid hold of the heroes, who there did not abandon Droṇa, and what mean-spirited men fled away in terror?

sanskrit: ke vā tatra tanūs tyaktvā pratīpaṃ mṛtyum āvrajan amānuṣāṇāṃ jetāraṃ yuddheṣv api dhanaṃjayam
english: Or who there, casting away their bodies, went forth to meet death head-on against Dhanaṃjaya, the conqueror even of more-than-human foes in battle?

sanskrit: na ca vegaṃ sitāśvasya viśakṣyantīha māmakāḥ gāṇḍīvasya ca nirghoṣaṃ prāvṛḍjaladanisvanam
english: My men cannot endure the onset of him whose horses are white, nor the roar of the Gāṇḍīva, like the rumble of the rain-clouds of the monsoon.

sanskrit: viṣvakseno yasya yantā yoddhā caiva dhanaṃjayaḥ aśakyaḥ sa ratho jetuṃ manye devāsurair api
english: That chariot whose driver is Viṣvaksena and whose warrior is Dhanaṃjaya is, I think, impossible to conquer even by gods and demons together.

sanskrit: sukumāro yuvā śūro darśanīyaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ medhāvī nipuṇo dhīmān yudhi satyaparākramaḥ
english: Delicate, young, heroic, and fair to behold is that son of Pāṇḍu, intelligent, skilled, wise, of true valor in battle —

sanskrit: ārāvaṃ vipulaṃ kurvan vyathayan sarvakauravān yadāyān nakulo dhīmān ke śūrāḥ paryavārayan
english: when the wise Nakula advanced, raising a vast war-cry and dismaying all the Kauravas, what heroes hemmed him in?

sanskrit: āśīviṣa iva kruddhaḥ sahadevo yadābhyayāt śatrūṇāṃ kadanaṃ kurvañ jetāsau durjayo yudhi
english: When Sahadeva, enraged like a venomous serpent, came on, wreaking havoc among the foes — that hard-to-conquer one, a victor in battle —

sanskrit: āryavratam amogheṣuṃ hrīmantam aparājitam droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ ke śūrāḥ paryavārayan
english: as he advanced toward Droṇa — that man of noble vows, whose arrows never miss, modest and unconquered — what heroes hemmed him in?

sanskrit: yaḥ sa sauvīrarājasya pramathya mahatīṃ camūm ādatta mahiṣīṃ bhojyāṃ kāmyāṃ sarvāṅgaśobhanām
english: He who, having crushed the great host of the Sauvīra king, carried off his cherished and desirable queen, lovely in every limb —

sanskrit: satyaṃ dhṛtiś ca śauryaṃ ca brahmacaryaṃ ca kevalam sarvāṇi yuyudhāne 'smin nityāni puruṣarṣabhe
english: truth, firmness, valor, and perfect continence — all these dwell forever in this Yuyudhāna, this bull among men.

sanskrit: balinaṃ satyakarmāṇam adīnam aparājitam vāsudevasamaṃ yuddhe vāsudevād anantaram
english: Strong, true in deed, undaunted, unconquered, equal to Vāsudeva in battle and second only to Vāsudeva —

sanskrit: yuktaṃ dhanaṃjayapreṣye śūram ācāryakarmaṇi pārthena samam astreṣu kas taṃ droṇād avārayat
english: that hero ready in Dhanaṃjaya's service, skilled in a teacher's office, equal to Pārtha in weapons — who held him back from Droṇa?

sanskrit: vṛṣṇīnāṃ pravaraṃ vīraṃ śūraṃ sarvadhanuṣmatām rāmeṇa samam astreṣu yaśasā vikrameṇa ca
english: The foremost hero of the Vṛṣṇis, valiant among all bowmen, the equal of Rāma in weapons, in fame, and in prowess —

sanskrit: satyaṃ dhṛtir damaḥ śauryaṃ brahmacaryam anuttamam sātvate tāni sarvāṇi trailokyam iva keśave
english: truth, firmness, self-restraint, valor, and continence unsurpassed — all these are present in that Sātvata, as the three worlds are present in Keśava.

sanskrit: tam evaṃguṇasaṃpannaṃ durvāram api daivataiḥ samāsādya maheṣvāsaṃ ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: That great archer, endowed with such qualities, hard to ward off even by the gods — what heroes closed in and hemmed him round?

sanskrit: pāñcāleṣūttamaṃ śūram uttamābhijanapriyam nityam uttamakarmāṇam uttamaujasam āhave
english: The foremost hero among the Pāñcālas, beloved for his noble birth, ever doing the highest deeds, of supreme energy in battle —

sanskrit: yuktaṃ dhanaṃjayahite mamānarthāya cottamam yamavaiśravaṇādityamahendravaruṇopamam
english: devoted to Dhanaṃjaya's welfare and the foremost cause of my ruin, the equal of Yama, Vaiśravaṇa, Āditya, great Indra, and Varuṇa —

sanskrit: mahārathasamākhyātaṃ droṇāyodyantam āhave tyajantaṃ tumule prāṇān ke śūrāḥ paryavārayan
english: renowned as a mighty chariot-warrior, rising up against Droṇa in battle and ready to lay down his life in the tumult — what heroes hemmed him in?
